mainTopic: רבי יוסי and the חכמים on פיגול spreading between מתירין and between parts, plus רבי ינאי's rule on a זר gathering the לבונה
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: רבי יוסי agrees a מנחה is פיגול when the intent was to burn the קומץ tomorrow. If the intent was to burn the לבונה tomorrow, he says it is only פסול. ריש לקיש explains that in his view one מתיר cannot make another מתיר פיגול, even two cups of the same לבונה. The גמרא shows that רבי יוסי's words 'the לבונה is not from the מנחה' mean the קומץ does not hold back the לבונה. The רבנן answer that two items fixed in one כלי count as one. Next, רבי ינאי rules that a זר who gathers the לבונה makes the מנחה פסול, because gathering counts as הולכה. רב מרי tries to prove this from the משנה about placing the קומץ in a כלי, but the גמרא rejects the proof: placing in a כלי simply matches קבלה. A new משנה brings רבי יוסי and the חכמים arguing about a פיגול thought on only one of two loaves or arrangements. רב הונא extends רבי יוסי's view to the two thighs of one animal, and רב נחמן begins a challenge from a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה teaches that רבי יוסי agrees in this case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier discussion. The משנה's words 'רבי יוסי agrees' are there to teach that he agrees the מנחה is פיגול when the intent was to burn the קומץ tomorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us that in this case he agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up an earlier question. It explains that the משנה bothered to say רבי יוסי 'agrees' so we would know he holds פיגול in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a קמיצה done with the intent to burn the קומץ tomorrow. That intent touches only one of the two מתירין, the קומץ and not the לבונה. Since רבי יוסי still calls it פיגול, we learn he holds that intent about half of the מתירין can create פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (a new point we would not have known otherwise)
Agrees, concedes
An offering made unfit by a wrong-time intention. Eating it carries כרת.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי agrees that intent to burn the קומץ tomorrow makes the מנחה פיגול. So when he says 'no פיגול' in the next case, the reason must be something else.

phrases.english: It teaches us
that in this case he agrees.
phrases.notes: 'This case' is the one in the משנה where the intent was to burn the קומץ tomorrow. 'He' is רבי יוסי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion that began before this section, about why the משנה says 'רבי יוסי agrees'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's wording teaches that רבי יוסי holds intent to burn the קומץ tomorrow creates פיגול, even though it involves only one מתיר.

steps.title: משנה: intent to burn the frankincense tomorrow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה. If the intent was to burn the לבונה tomorrow, רבי יוסי rules the מנחה פסול, but there is no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the intent was to burn its frankincense tomorrow, רבי יוסי says: it is unfit, and there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a new line from the משנה so it can explain it. Here the wrong-time intent is about the לבונה, not the קומץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'פסול but no כרת' means the offering is ruined, but it is not real פיגול. Real פיגול would bring כרת for eating it. This seems surprising, since in the last step רבי יוסי did call it פיגול when the intent was about the קומץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Frankincense, burned on the מזבח together with the קומץ of a מנחה
Tomorrow, past the time allowed for the offering
Unfit, invalid
Spiritual 'cutting off', the punishment for eating פיגול

phrases.english: With the intent to burn its frankincense tomorrow,
Rabbi Yosei says:
it is unfit, and there is no karet for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהַקְטִיר לְבוֹנָתָהּ לְמָחָר, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה. Step 1 already showed that the 'no פיגול' here cannot be because the intent involved only half the מתירין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יוסי's view, intent to burn the לבונה tomorrow makes the מנחה פסול but not פיגול, so there is no כרת.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: one permitting part does not make another into פיגול
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains רבי יוסי's reason. While doing the service of one מתיר, a wrong-time intent about a different מתיר does not create פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: רבי יוסי used to say that a מתיר does not make another מתיר פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the reason behind רבי יוסי's ruling from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two items 'permit' the מנחה: the קומץ and the לבונה. Taking the קומץ is a service of one מתיר, but the bad intent was about the other one, the לבונה. רבי יוסי holds that intent about a different מתיר cannot create פיגול. That is why the result is only פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: A permitting part: an item whose offering on the מזבח allows the rest of the קרבן to be eaten
Makes something into פיגול

steps.confusionAlert: Step 1 showed that רבי יוסי does create פיגול from intent about just one of the two מתירין, as long as the intent is about the same item being worked on (the קומץ). His problem here is different: the intent was about the other מתיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how רבי יוסי can rule פיגול in the קומץ case but no פיגול in the לבונה case.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Rabbi Yosei used to say,
a permitting factor does not render the permitting factor piggul.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רבי יוסי's ruling quoted in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יוסי's view, intent during the service of one מתיר about another מתיר does not create פיגול.

steps.title: The same rule for the two bowls of frankincense of the showbread
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש extends the rule to the two cups of לבונה offered with the לחם הפנים. Burning one cup with intent to burn the other tomorrow does not create פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you say the same about the two cups of frankincense of the לחם הפנים: one מתיר does not make another מתיר פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש applies רבי יוסי's rule to a second case, the לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cups of לבונה are burned to permit the לחם הפנים, so each cup is a מתיר. If the כהן burns one cup intending to burn the other tomorrow, the intent is about a different מתיר. So, by the same rule, there is no פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: And you say the same (the same rule applies)
The cups of frankincense placed with the לחם הפנים
The showbread on the שולחן in the משכן and מקדש

phrases.english: And you would say the same

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁנֵי בְּזִיכֵי לְבוֹנָה שֶׁל לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים,
phrases.english: with regard to the two bowls of frankincense of the shewbread,
that a permitting factor does not render the permitting factor piggul.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בִּשְׁנֵי בְּזִיכֵי לְבוֹנָה שֶׁל לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues ריש לקיש's statement and applies its rule to a parallel case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning one cup of לבונה of the לחם הפנים with intent to burn the other tomorrow does not create פיגול.

steps.title: Why add the case of the showbread?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש needed to add 'and you say the same.' The rule seems to apply to the second case obviously.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and you say the same'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why ריש לקיש's extra line is needed. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one מתיר never makes another מתיר פיגול, the two cups should be included automatically. So the גמרא wants to know what new point the extra line teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: What? Here: what does this add?

phrases.english: What is the point of: "And you would say the same"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the addition in step 4 was needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new idea does the לחם הפנים case teach beyond the basic rule?

steps.title: Two bowls of the same kind still don't make each other פיגול
steps.stepSummary: Without this line we might have thought רבי יוסי's reason was that לבונה is a different material from the flour of the מנחה. Two cups of לבונה are the same kind and might make each other פיגול. ריש לקיש teaches that they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that רבי יוסי's reason with the לבונה is that it is a different kind from the מנחה. But two cups of לבונה are the same kind, so say they make each other פיגול. So ריש לקיש teaches us that they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. It shows the mistaken idea we might have had, which the extra line rules out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One possible reading of רבי יוסי is that the קומץ cannot make the לבונה פיגול because they are different substances, flour and frankincense. On that reading, two cups of לבונה, which are the same material, would make each other פיגול. ריש לקיש's extra line rejects this: the real rule is that any מתיר cannot make another מתיר פיגול, whether the material is the same or not.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken idea to be rejected)
Its kind, the same type of material
One another
They make into פיגול

steps.whatToRemember: In ריש לקיש's explanation of רבי יוסי, the reason is that one מתיר never makes another מתיר פיגול. Being a different material is not the reason, so even two cups of the same לבונה cannot make each other פיגול.

phrases.english: Lest you say
that the reason of Rabbi Yosei with the frankincense
is because it is not the same type as the meal offering,
but with the two bowls of frankincense,
which are the same type as each other,
say they do render one another piggul,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בִּלְבוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra line rules out the idea that רבי יוסי's reason is about different materials. Even two cups of the same לבונה, each a מתיר, do not make each other פיגול.

steps.title: The end of the משנה seems to say לבונה is a different kind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 6. The סיפא of the משנה shows רבי יוסי telling the רבנן that לבונה 'is not from the מנחה.' That sounds exactly like the 'different kind' reason that Step 6 said was not his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say רבי יוסי's reason is not that לבונה is a different kind from the מנחה? The end of the משנה says: The רבנן asked him, 'How is this different from a זבח?' He answered, 'With a זבח, the blood, meat and altar parts are all one. But the לבונה is not part of the מנחה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea from Step 6 by quoting the end of the משנה. There רבי יוסי himself seems to give the 'different kind' reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said רבי יוסי's reason is not that לבונה differs in kind from flour, since even two cups of לבונה do not make each other פיגול. But in the סיפא, רבי יוסי contrasts a זבח, whose parts are 'one,' with לבונה, which 'is not from the מנחה.' That sounds like a difference of kind, so the explanation in Step 6 seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter part of a משנה or ברייתא
An animal offering
The fats and parts of an animal offering that are burned on the מזבח
Its own kind or type

phrases.english: And can you really say
that the reason of Rabbi Yosei regarding the frankincense

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּלָאו מִינַהּ דְּמִנְחָה הִיא?
phrases.english: is not because it is not the same kind as the meal offering?
But it is taught in the latter clause:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מָה שִׁינְּתָה מִן הַזֶּבַח?
phrases.english: They said to him: How is it different from an animal offering?
He said to them: An animal offering,
its blood, its meat and its altar parts are all one,
but the frankincense is not part of the meal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 6 that רבי יוסי's reason is not that לבונה is a different kind from the מנחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the סיפא, רבי יוסי himself says the לבונה 'is not from the מנחה,' which sounds like a difference of kind.

steps.title: 'Not part of the מנחה' means the קומץ does not hold back the לבונה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads רבי יוסי's words in a new way. 'Not from the מנחה' does not mean a different kind. It means the לבונה does not depend on the קומץ. Either one may be burned first.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'not from the מנחה' mean? It means the לבונה is not held back by the מנחה. The קומץ holds back the שירים: until the קומץ is burned, the שירים cannot be eaten. The קומץ does not hold back the לבונה in that way. The כהן may burn whichever one he wants first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what רבי יוסי really meant. He was talking about order, not about a difference of kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שירים cannot be eaten until the קומץ is burned, so they depend on it. The לבונה does not depend on the קומץ, since either may go on the מזבח first. That makes the לבונה its own separate מתיר. So Step 6 still stands: the reason is 'separate מתיר,' not 'different material.'

keyTerms.meaning: Holding back; one thing must happen before another is allowed
The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
The rest of the מנחה, eaten by the כהנים
Burns on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'אינה מן המנחה' as 'it is a different substance.' Here the גמרא says it means the לבונה does not have to wait for the קומץ.

phrases.english: What does 'it is not part of the meal offering' mean?
It is not part of the holding-back of the meal offering,
meaning: it is not that just as it holds back
(the handful holds back the remainder),
so that as long as the handful has not been burned
the remainder may not be eaten,
so too it holds back the frankincense;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי בָּעֵי הַאי מַקְטַר בְּרֵישָׁא
phrases.english: rather, if he wants he burns this one first,
and if he wants he burns that one first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not from the מנחה' means לבונה is a different kind of material.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the לבונה does not wait for the קומץ, so it is a separate מתיר.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי, the קומץ and לבונה are two separate מתירים because either can be burned first. A thought about one during the service of the other does not create פיגול.

steps.title: The רבנן: things fixed in one כלי count as one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the רבנן, who do say פיגול in this case. The rule that one מתיר cannot make another פיגול, as with the two lambs, applies only when they were not fixed in one כלי. The קומץ and לבונה were in one כלי, so they count as one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They say that 'one מתיר does not make another פיגול' applies to a case like slaughtering one lamb with the plan to eat from the other tomorrow, where both stay כשר. That is only when they were never fixed in one כלי. When they were fixed in one כלי, they count as one thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן would reply to רבי יוסי's logic and answers for them. They draw a line between separate items and items set together in one כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן agree that one מתיר usually cannot make another פיגול, as in the case of the two lambs. But the קומץ and the לבונה sat together in one כלי. That joins them into one unit, so a wrong-time thought about one makes the whole מנחה פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: One permitting item cannot make another permitting item פיגול
Lambs; here, the two lambs offered with the שתי הלחם on שבועות
They were fixed together in one כלי
They are treated like one

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out the real point of the argument. Both sides accept the rule about separate מתירים. They disagree only on whether sharing one כלי makes two items into one.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how the רבנן, who say this is פיגול, would answer.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָמְרִינַן ״אֵין מַתִּיר מְפַגֵּל אֶת הַמַּתִּיר״
phrases.english: When we say 'a permitting item does not make another permitting item פיגול'
(regarding one who slaughtered one of the lambs
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: intending to eat from the other one tomorrow,
where you said both are fit),

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא אִיקְּבַעוּ בְּחַד מָנָא,
phrases.english: that applies only where they were not fixed in one vessel,
but where they were fixed in one vessel,
they are like one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי יוסי's reasoning to the view of the רבנן who disagree
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן can say פיגול if one מתיר does not make another פיגול
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: That rule applies only to items not fixed in one כלי; the קומץ and לבונה were, so they count as one
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי says the קומץ and לבונה are separate, so there is no פיגול. The רבנן say sharing one כלי makes them one, so there is פיגול.

steps.title: Gathering the לבונה by a non-כהן makes the מנחה פסול
steps.stepSummary: A new topic about לבונה. רבי ינאי rules that if a זר gathers the לבונה off the מנחה, it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: If a non-כהן gathers the לבונה, it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new statement about the לבונה. רבי ינאי says a זר may not gather it up from the מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gathering the לבונה from the top of the מנחה might seem like simple prep work that anyone could do. רבי ינאי says it is treated as a real עבודה, so a זר doing it makes the מנחה פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Gathering or collecting
A non-כהן
Invalid, disqualified

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:
Gathering the frankincense by a non-priest is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: לִיקּוּט לְבוֹנָה בְּזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to לבונה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a זר gathers the לבונה, the מנחה is פסול.

steps.title: Why is gathering by a non-כהן פסול?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי ינאי's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why gathering would matter at all. It is setting up רבי ירמיה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gathering is not one of the four main עבודות of a מנחה. So the גמרא wants to know what makes it count as an עבודה that only a כהן may do.

keyTerms.meaning: Reason

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why gathering the לבונה by a זר makes the מנחה פסול

steps.title: Gathering counts as part of הולכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה explains that gathering the לבונה is already part of הולכה. רבי ינאי holds that moving it without walking still counts as הולכה, and הולכה by a זר is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It is because the עבודה of הולכה has touched it. רבי ינאי holds that carrying without moving one's feet is still called הולכה, and הולכה by a זר is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives the reason for רבי ינאי's rule. Gathering the לבונה counts as the start of carrying it to the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking the לבונה up moves it toward the מזבח, even if the person does not take a step. רבי ינאי holds that this movement already counts as הולכה. Since הולכה is an עבודה that must be done by a כהן, a זר who gathers the לבונה makes the מנחה פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying the offering toward the מזבח, one of the עבודות
Touched it; here, it is already part of that עבודה
Without moving one's feet
He holds (this opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ינאי, moving an item toward the מזבח counts as הולכה even without walking. That is why gathering the לבונה must be done by a כהן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
Because the service of carrying has touched it,
phrases.notes: He means the gathering is already counted as part of carrying it to the מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר הוֹלָכָה שֶׁלֹּא בָּרֶגֶל שְׁמָהּ הוֹלָכָה,
phrases.english: he holds that carrying without moving the feet is called carrying,
and carrying by a non-priest is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: מִשּׁוּם הוֹלָכָה נָגְעוּ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Gathering counts as הולכה, since even carrying without walking is הולכה, and הולכה by a זר is פסול.

steps.title: רב מרי brings support from the משנה's list of מנחה services
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי says a משנה already supports רבי ינאי's idea, and he quotes the four services of a מנחה that it lists.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: We have also learned this in a משנה. 'This is the rule: anyone who takes the קומץ, or places it in a כלי, or carries it, or burns it...'
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי opens a proof for רבי ינאי by quoting a משנה. This step only sets up the proof; the next steps explain how it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists four services of a מנחה where a wrong intention matters. The key item is 'placing in a כלי'. רב מרי will use it to show that a step that does not look like a main service can still count as an important עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
Takes the handful of flour from the מנחה
Places the קומץ into a holy vessel
Carries it to the מזבח
Burns it on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:
We too have learned this in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: He means a משנה earlier in the מסכת (12a) that teaches when a מנחה becomes פיגול.

phrases.english: This is the rule:
Anyone who takes the handful, or places it in a vessel,
or carries it, or burns it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to support רבי ירמיה's explanation of רבי ינאי.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ינאי's rule that gathering the לבונה is a real עבודה (הולכה)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing קומץ, נותן בכלי, מוליך, מקטיר

steps.title: Which animal service does 'placing in a vessel' match?
steps.stepSummary: Three of the מנחה services clearly match animal-offering services. The גמרא asks what 'placing in a כלי' matches.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that taking the קומץ is like שחיטה, carrying is like carrying the blood, and burning is like sprinkling the blood. But placing in a כלי, what service is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא matches each מנחה service to an animal-offering service and finds one left without a clear match. It is setting up the main point of the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animal offerings have four services: שחיטה, קבלה, הולכה, זריקה. קומץ matches שחיטה, מוליך matches הולכה, and מקטיר matches זריקה. 'Placing in a כלי' needs a partner, and the obvious one, קבלה, does not seem to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted
Slaughters the animal
Sprinkles the blood on the מזבח
What service is he doing?

phrases.english: It makes sense that taking the handful is like slaughtering;
carrying is also like carrying,
phrases.notes: Carrying the קומץ to the מזבח matches carrying the blood to the מזבח.

phrases.english: burning is like sprinkling;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא נוֹתֵן בִּכְלִי מַאי קָא עָבֵיד?
phrases.english: but placing it in a vessel, what service is he doing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the משנה quoted in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which animal-offering service 'placing the קומץ in a כלי' matches

steps.title: Placing in a vessel is not truly like receiving blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests it matches קבלה, then rejects that, because blood flows into the כלי by itself while the קומץ is placed in by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is like קבלה, are they really alike? There, the blood flows in by itself. Here, he picks it up and puts it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the obvious answer, that placing in a כלי is like קבלה, and pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קבלה the כהן just holds the כלי and the blood flows in. With the מנחה, the כהן actively takes the קומץ and puts it in. Because the actions are so different, the simple match fails.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say
Receiving the animal's blood in a holy vessel
Is it really similar?
By itself, without action
Takes and throws in

phrases.english: If you say it is because it is like receiving the blood,
is it really similar?
There, it comes in by itself;
phrases.notes: The blood flows from the animal straight into the כלי.

phrases.english: here, he takes it and throws it in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּדָמֵי לְקַבָּלָה, מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects a possible answer to step 14's question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The simple comparison of נותן בכלי to קבלה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: קבלה happens passively, but placing the קומץ is an active act.

steps.title: A step that cannot be skipped is an important service
steps.stepSummary: Placing in a כלי is a step the offering cannot go without, so it is an important עבודה and is treated like קבלה anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since there is no way to skip doing it, it is an important עבודה. So it is necessarily treated like קבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real reason that 'placing in a כלי' counts as a service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is not that the action looks like קבלה. It is that the offering cannot be brought without it. A necessary step is an important עבודה, and that is why it takes the place of קבלה.

keyTerms.term: לָא סַגִּיא לֵיהּ דְּלָא עָבֵד לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: There is no way to manage without doing it
An important, significant service
Necessarily, by force

phrases.english: Rather, it is because, since

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא סַגִּיא לֵיהּ דְּלָא עָבֵד לַהּ,
phrases.english: there is no way to manage without doing it,
it is an important service,
so necessarily it is treated like receiving the blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּכֵיוָן דְּלָא סַגִּיא לֵיהּ דְּלָא עָבֵד לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A step without which the offering cannot be brought is an important עבודה, so it counts as קבלה.

steps.title: So too, gathering the לבונה counts as הולכה
steps.stepSummary: Using the same logic, gathering the לבונה is a step that cannot be skipped, so it is an important עבודה treated like הולכה. This supports רבי ינאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, since there is no way to skip gathering the לבונה, it is an important עבודה. So it is necessarily treated like הולכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי applies the rule from the משנה to רבי ינאי's case and finishes his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gathering the לבונה may not look like real carrying. But the לבונה cannot be offered without being gathered, so it is an important עבודה. It counts as הולכה, and a זר doing it makes the מנחה פסול, just as רבי ינאי ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, in our case
Carrying the offering to the מזבח
Frankincense placed on the מנחה

steps.whatToRemember: רב מרי's proof says a step the offering cannot go without counts as a real עבודה, so gathering the לבונה counts as הולכה. Steps 18-19 reject this proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the proposed test, that a step counts as an עבודה if it is necessary. The next steps reject it as the reason behind the משנה.

phrases.english: Here too,
phrases.notes: Here means רבי ינאי's case of gathering the לבונה off the מנחה.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא סַגִּיא לֵהּ דְּלָא עָבֵד לַהּ,
phrases.english: since there is no way to manage without doing it,
it is an important service,

phrases.aramaic: עַל כֻּרְחָיךְ מְשַׁוֵּי לַהּ כִּי הוֹלָכָה.
phrases.english: so necessarily it is treated like carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא סַגִּיא לֵהּ דְּלָא עָבֵד לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 16's rule to רבי ינאי's case.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ינאי's ruling that a זר gathering the לבונה makes the מנחה פסול
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's treating נותן בכלי as an important עבודה like קבלה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Proposed proof: gathering the לבונה is a necessary step, so it counts as הולכה. Steps 18-19 reject this proof.

steps.title: No, placing in a vessel really is like collecting blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof for רבי ינאי. It says placing the קומץ in a כלי truly matches קבלה, so we never needed the 'cannot be skipped' reason. It then begins to answer the earlier difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. In truth, placing in a vessel is like collecting the blood. And as for what bothered you, that there the blood flows in by itself while here he picks it up and throws it in:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls back the proof for רבי ינאי. It goes back to the first idea, that placing in a כלי matches קבלה. The next line will explain why the earlier difficulty is not a real problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17's proof depended on the idea that placing in a כלי counts as an עבודה only because the offering cannot go without it. If placing in a כלי simply matches קבלה, that reason is not needed. Without it, there is no basis to say gathering the לבונה is an important עבודה, so the support for רבי ינאי falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / in truth: a return to an earlier position
That it is similar to
By itself, on its own
Takes and throws (puts in by hand)

steps.confusionAlert: This 'לא' rejects the reason given in step 16, that placing in a כלי counts because 'it cannot be skipped.' That is the reason step 17 relied on. The גמרא goes back to the plain comparison to קבלה that step 15 had pushed away, and now defends it.

phrases.english: No, actually it is because it is similar to collecting [the blood],
and as for what was difficult for you:
there [the blood flows into the vessel] by itself,
here he takes [the קומץ] and throws it in —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 17 by going back to the plain comparison to קבלה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof for רבי ינאי from the idea that gathering the לבונה is an important step.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Placing in a כלי counts because it really matches קבלה, not because it 'cannot be skipped'. So nothing follows about gathering the לבונה.

steps.title: Both are about the vessel making it holy
steps.stepSummary: Collecting the blood and placing the קומץ both involve the holiness of a כלי. So it does not matter whether the item gets in by itself or by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, both of them are about the holiness of the vessel. What difference does it make to me whether it goes in by itself or he picks it up and throws it in?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the difficulty from step 15. What counts is that the כלי makes the item holy, not how the item got into it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said the two are different because blood flows in by itself while the קומץ is put in by hand. Here the גמרא says that difference does not matter. The important point is the same in both cases: the כלי makes the item holy and ready for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: After all / now consider
Holiness given by a holy כלי
What difference does it make to me

steps.whatToRemember: Placing the קומץ in a כלי is just like קבלה, because both are about the כלי making the item holy. So the proof for רבי ינאי from gathering the לבונה falls away.

phrases.english: After all, both of them are [about] the holiness of a vessel,
what difference is it to me if it goes in by itself,
or if he takes it and throws it in?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes step 18 by answering the difficulty it quoted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the difference raised earlier does not matter.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood falling in by itself is not like the קומץ put in by hand, so placing in a כלי cannot match קבלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are about the holiness of the כלי, so how the item got in does not matter.

steps.title: New משנה: a פיגול thought about only one loaf or one arrangement, and רבי יוסי's view
steps.stepSummary: Someone performed the service with a thought to eat only one of the two loaves, or one of the two arrangements, the next day. רבי יוסי says only that one is פיגול with כרת. The other is פסול but has no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughtered the two lambs with the thought of eating one of the loaves the next day, or burned the two bowls of frankincense with the thought of eating one of the arrangements the next day, רבי יוסי says: the loaf or arrangement he had in mind is פיגול and one gets כרת for eating it. The second one is פסול but has no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks what happens when the wrong-time thought was about only one of two items that come together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבועות, the two lambs make the two loaves permitted. With לחם הפנים, burning the two bowls of לבונה makes the two arrangements permitted. רבי יוסי says the פיגול thought only affects the item he thought about. The other one is still ruined (פסול), but it is not full פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering ruined by a thought to eat it after its allowed time; eating it brings כרת
Being 'cut off', a heavenly punishment
The bowls of לבונה placed with לחם הפנים
The two arrangements (rows) of לחם הפנים
Loaves (here the two loaves of שבועות)
Invalid, not allowed to be eaten

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If one slaughtered the two lambs
phrases.notes: These are the two lambs that come with the two loaves on שבועות.

phrases.english: with the thought to eat one of the loaves the next day,
[or] burned the two bowls [of frankincense]
with the thought to eat one of the arrangements the next day,
Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתָהּ הַחַלָּה וְאוֹתוֹ הַסֵּדֶר שֶׁחִישֵּׁב עָלָיו –
phrases.english: that loaf and that arrangement which he had in mind —
is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for it,
and the second one is invalid, but there is no כרת for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁחַט שְׁנֵי כְּבָשִׂים לֶאֱכוֹל אַחַת מִן הַחַלּוֹת לְמָחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, פיגול affects only the item he thought about. The other item is פסול without כרת.

steps.title: חכמים: both become פיגול
steps.stepSummary: חכמים argue with רבי יוסי. They say both loaves, or both arrangements, are פיגול and bring כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: both this one and that one are פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the other side of the argument. A thought about one item makes both items פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים see the two loaves, or the two arrangements, as one unit that is made permitted together. So a פיגול thought about one of them spreads to both, and eating either one brings כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one: both

steps.whyThisMatters: This argument about whether פיגול spreads from one part to the whole sets up the גמרא's discussion that comes next.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
this one and that one are פיגול
and one is liable to כרת for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opinion that argues with רבי יוסי in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פיגול thought about one of the pair makes both פיגול with כרת.

steps.title: רב הונא: in רבי יוסי's view, פיגול on the right thigh does not spread to the left
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reports that רבי יוסי also held this about a single animal. A פיגול thought about the right thigh does not make the left thigh פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: רבי יוסי used to say that if someone had a פיגול thought about the right thigh, the left thigh did not become פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב הונא taking רבי יוסי's view further. It now applies even to two parts of one animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the case was two separate loaves or arrangements. רב הונא says רבי יוסי applies the same idea inside one animal. A thought about one part does not spread to another part, so the left thigh is not פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Had a פיגול thought about (it)
Thigh (of the animal)
Became פיגול

steps.confusionAlert: This goes beyond the משנה. The משנה spoke about two separate items, but here it is two parts of the very same animal.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Huna says:
Rabbi Yosei would say:
[if] he had a פיגול thought about the right thigh —
the left thigh has not become פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, פִּיגֵּל בַּיָּרֵךְ שֶׁל יָמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבי יוסי's view in the משנה and applies it to parts of one animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, a פיגול thought about one thigh does not make the other thigh פיגול.

steps.title: What is the reason? Logic or a verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי holds this way. It says the reason can come either from logic or from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? If you want, say it is logic, and if you want, say it comes from a verse.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יוסי's view and says two explanations are coming, one from logic and one from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא lays out two possible sources for the rule but does not explain them yet. The next lines will spell out the logic first and then the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
If you wish, say...
A logical reason
A verse (פסוק)

phrases.english: What is the reason?
If you wish, say a logical reason,
and if you wish, say a verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רב הונא's statement of רבי יוסי's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a פיגול thought about one thigh does not spread to the other in רבי יוסי's view.

steps.title: The logical reason: a thought is no stronger than real impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי's view can come from logic. If one limb becomes טמא, the whole animal does not become טמא. So a פיגול thought about one part should not spread to another part either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it comes from logic: a thought cannot be stronger than real impurity. If one limb became impure, would the whole animal become impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 23 with the first option: a reason based on logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real טומאה that touches one limb stays on that limb. A פיגול thought is only a thought, so it should not do more than real טומאה does. That is why a thought about the right thigh does not reach the left thigh.

keyTerms.meaning: Logic, a reasoned argument
Intent, a thought during the service (here, a פיגול thought)
Ritual impurity
A limb or body part

phrases.english: If you wish, say it is from logic:
Intent is no stronger
than an actual case of impurity.
If one limb became impure,
would the whole thing become impure?
phrases.notes: This question expects the answer no. Only the limb that touched the impurity is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first of the two answers promised in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פיגול thought is no stronger than real טומאה, which does not spread from one limb to the whole animal.

steps.title: The verse reason: 'of it' and not from the other part
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי's view can also come from a פסוק. The word ממנו ('of it') teaches that only the part that was made פיגול brings punishment, not the other part.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it comes from a verse: "And the soul that eats of it shall bear its sin." 'Of it,' and not from the other one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second answer to step 23: a source from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about פיגול says the person who eats 'of it' (ממנו) is punished. The גמרא reads this as limiting the punishment to the specific part that was made פיגול, and not its fellow part.

keyTerms.meaning: A verse in the תורה
'Of it,' read here as limiting the punishment to that specific part
'Shall bear its sin,' meaning will be punished (here, כרת)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי has two sources: logic (a thought is no stronger than real טומאה) and the פסוק (ממנו, not its fellow). For him, each part stands alone.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it is from a verse:
"And the soul that eats of it
shall bear its sin" —
"of it," and not from its fellow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second, alternative answer to the same question in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ממנו in ויקרא 7:18 limits the punishment to the part that was made פיגול.

steps.title: רב נחמן quotes a ברייתא: both loaves together for a כזית
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן brings a ברייתא: there is no כרת unless the פיגול thought covers both loaves together for a כזית. This suggests a thought about both counts, but a thought about only one does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן challenged רב הונא: "And the חכמים say, there is never כרת until he has a פיגול thought about both of them for a כזית." Both of them, yes. One of them, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן starts a challenge against רב הונא by quoting a ברייתא and drawing an inference from it. The גמרא is setting up the next moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא requires one כזית made up from both loaves together. The inference is that a thought about both loaves works, but a thought about only one does not. The גמרא will now work out whose view this is.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual 'cutting off,' the punishment for eating פיגול
An offering ruined by a thought of eating it at the wrong time
An olive-size, the minimum amount that counts
Yes / no

steps.confusionAlert: The 'חכמים' in this ברייתא are not the חכמים of step 21. The גמרא is about to show that this ברייתא actually follows רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman challenged Rav Huna:
And the Sages say,
there is never כרת
until he has a פיגול thought about both of them for an olive-size.
phrases.notes: He means one olive-size altogether, made up from the two loaves combined.

phrases.english: Both of them: yes.
One of them: no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an attack on רב הונא's report in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's report that for רבי יוסי, a פיגול thought on one thigh does not affect the other thigh.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the ברייתא allows combining both loaves into one כזית. This will be used to show the parts are treated as connected.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא? It must be רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא cannot follow the רבנן of the משנה, since for them even a thought about one loaf would be enough. So it must follow רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say the רבנן, then even one of them should also be enough! Rather, it is obviously רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן works out which תנא the ברייתא follows, as a step in his challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן (step 21) hold that a thought about one loaf makes both loaves פיגול. So the ברייתא's ruling, 'one of them, no,' cannot be theirs. It must be רבי יוסי's.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whose is it?', asking which תנא a teaching follows
'If you say,' introducing an option that will be rejected
'Obviously,' it is clear

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
If you say it is the Rabbis,
then even with one of them it should also count!
Rather, it is obviously Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the ברייתא from step 26 to make the challenge work.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It must be רבי יוסי, since the Rabbis would not require both loaves.

steps.title: If the two thighs are one body, mixed intent about the loaves can combine
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן begins his point: if the two thighs of one animal count as one body, it makes sense that mixed intent about the two loaves combines into one כזית. The rest of the argument continues next.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works fine if you say it is one body. That is why it combines.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן starts the core of his challenge. The sentence continues past this point, so the גמרא is still building the attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "One body" here means the two thighs of ONE ANIMAL, not the two loaves. If רבי יוסי held that the two thighs are one body, so that פיגול intent about one thigh reaches the other, it would make sense that one mixed intent, half a כזית from each loaf, combines into a full כזית: joining the two loaves in one thought makes them count as if they came from one body (רש״י). This does not mean that intent about one loaf on its own affects the other loaf. The loaves do not come from one body, and the ברייתא itself says intent about only one of them does not make the other פיגול. The challenge is aimed at רב הונא, who said רבי יוסי treats the two thighs as separate.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It works fine if...', granting one side before asking about the other
One body, a single unit
Combines, joins together to reach the needed amount

phrases.english: It works fine if you say
that it is one body;
that is why it combines,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא חַד גּוּפָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the identification of רבי יוסי from step 27 to begin the actual challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim (step 22) that for רבי יוסי the parts of one animal are separate for פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mixed intent can join half a כזית from each of two separate loaves only if such a thought can make separate parts count as one body. That fits the view that the two thighs of one animal are one body, not רב הונא's report that רבי יוסי treats the thighs as two bodies.
